plan.title: Teaching fits what they're stuck on: a grounded tip, not a lecture

context.text: did my 10 min but the 2 ball thing is a mess, they keep crashing into each other
That's the hardest part, Casey, and you showed up for it. We'll work on it tomorrow.

transcript.text: Kalimera Casey! Those crashes are a normal part of learning two balls, so we're staying on it today at 6 pm in the living room, for 10 min. Here's the fix: throw ball 1 up to eye level, then throw ball 2 only when ball 1 hits its peak, so the second ball goes under the first and the two never meet. Slow and clean beats fast. You in?
ok I'm in but seriously how do I stop them crashing

Locked in, Casey. Crashes usually come from two things: throws that drift forward, and arcs at different heights. Here's the fix:

• Throw each ball up in a tall arc to eye level, not out in front of you.
• Aim every throw at the opposite shoulder, so the ball lands by the opposite hand at your hip.
• Keep your elbows at your sides and your hands at belt height.
• Throw ball 2 only when ball 1 peaks. That timing sends it under ball 1, not into it.

If they still collide, stop and do five clean one-ball arcs, then try again. For a visual, search YouTube for "learn to juggle 3 balls beginner cascade". See you at 6, and send a voice note on how the arcs go.
Hey Casey! Ten minutes to 6, so grab your two balls and clear a little space in the living room. Remember the peak rule: ball 2 goes only when ball 1 tops out. You've got this 💪
